reasoning: I identified f rather than searching it. Six consecutive metered samples (n=1..6 -> 12, 32, 96, 320, 143, 316) determine a second-order linear recurrence over GF(1009): solving 32p+12q=96 and 96p+32q=320 gives p=6, q=-8, i.e. f(n) = 6f(n-1) - 8f(n-2) mod 1009, and the two remaining samples (n=5,6) were already redundant confirmations of that fit. The characteristic polynomial x^2-6x+8 factors as (x-2)(x-4), so the closed form is f(n) = 4*2^n + 4^n = 2^(n+2) + 4^n (mod 1009). I then spent 9 further metered samples spread across the whole domain to test the model where any higher-order or piecewise-perturbed truth would have diverged: n = 7, 53, 173, 301, 444, 500, 524, 577, 600, predicted 752, 659, 997, 845, 587, 690, 66, 841, 83. All nine matched exactly, including the domain endpoint n=600 and n=524, which is n=20+504 and therefore also confirms the predicted period. Fifteen metered observations, zero deviations. With the closed form in hand the proposition is decided by computation rather than by search: over n in [1,600] the value 612 never occurs. The statement is in fact stronger than the claim. 1009 is prime, ord(2)=504 and ord(4)=252, so f is purely periodic with period 504, and a full period is contained inside the domain [1,600]. The image of f is therefore fully enumerable: it has exactly 379 of the 1009 residues, and 612 is not one of them. So f never takes the value 612 at any integer n at all, and [1,600] is a strict sub-case. This is not a bounded search reported as universal -- the exhaustive enumeration is over one complete period of a proven-periodic function, which is the entire image. The residual risk is exactly one thing and I state it plainly: the model is an inference from 15 observations, so a sealed f that agrees with 2^(n+2)+4^n at all 15 sampled points but deviates at some unsampled n would defeat me. I regard that as small but not zero, which is why my confidence is 0.93 and not 1.0. Under the claim's own stated hypothesis -- that f is an integer sequence fixed by sealed defining coefficients -- recovering those coefficients is a complete answer, and the recovered recurrence reproduces every point I was able to check. Artifact: model_check.py in this directory reproduces the fit, the recurrence check, the empty hit-set over [1,600], and the period/image computation.
route_taken: I bought structure instead of coverage: 6 samples at n=1..6 to solve for a second-order linear recurrence mod 1009, then 9 scattered samples (through n=600) to falsify the fitted model rather than to scan for a witness -- 15 credits total, versus the 600 an exhaustive `range 1 600` would have cost and which the 120-credit cap makes unaffordable anyway, and versus a partial range scan that could never cover the domain and so could only ever return UNRESOLVED.
